mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate reduces the cost of capital for corporations, leading to higher equity valuations and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days regardless of other conditions.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of instances when FEDFUNDS is below 1.5% over any 1-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate above 4.0% signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which typically leads to reduced consumer spending and corporate earnings, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: When UNRATE exceeds 4.0%, SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of cases over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicate a sharp contraction in consumer demand, which triggers a sell-off in equities, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: The joint decline in HOUST and RSAFS fails to predict negative SPX 20-day returns in more than 55% of cases over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production growth exceeds 1.5% year-over-year, the S&P 500 typically experiences positive returns over the next 60 trading days due to expanding corporate profits.
failure_condition: In periods where INDPRO YoY growth exceeds 1.5%, SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of cases over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly CPI inflation rate above 3.5% signals persistent inflation, prompting the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy, which leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: When CPIAUCSL exceeds 3.5%, SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) and a rise in unemployment (UNRATE) indicates a severe labor market contraction, which typically causes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint decline in PAYEMS and rise in UNRATE fails to predict negative SPX 5-day returns in more than 55% of cases over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A quarterly GDP growth rate above 2.0% (as measured by GDPC1) signals strong economic expansion, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: When GDPC1 quarterly growth exceeds 2.0%, SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of cases over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly housing starts (HOUST) decline exceeding 2.0% signals weakening consumer confidence and reduced construction activity, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: When HOUST declines by more than 2.0%, SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of cases over any 2-year rolling window.
